LESSON: METALLIC MATERIALS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Materials for Production
Topic 3.2: Metallic Materials
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Metallic Materials, part of Materials for Production in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: how to examine the physical properties of metallic materials. How are metallic materials used in day-to-day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Metallic Materials together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
31

• Digital Literacy: learner develops skills of interacting with technology when searching for information on metallic

materials.

• Communication and Collaboration: learner acquires speaking, listening, and teamwork skills when discussing the uses of

metallic materials.

Values:
• Unity: learner displays team spirit and collaboration with others while discussing the uses of metallic materials.

• Responsibility: learner shows accountability by caring for the print or digital media when searching for information on

metallic materials.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peer Education and Mentorship: the learner develops inter-personal relationships when performing practical activities to

examine the physical properties of metallic materials.

Link to Other Subjects:

Integrated Science: learner enhances knowledge on properties of materials during discussion of physical properties of metallic

materials.

• Digital devices such as; computer, laptop, smart phone, tablets among others
